title: A zero-dimensional closed subscheme of a finite-type scheme over a field is finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying topological space has dimension at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then the structure morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $Z$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], and $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].

proof.text: The closed immersion $Z\to X$ is of finite type because every closed immersion is proper, hence of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Since $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is of finite type by hypothesis, the composite structure morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is of finite type by the definition of finite-type morphism.

source.place: Tag 06LH (varieties-lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), algebraic case: a closed subscheme of a finite-type k-scheme is again algebraic

proof.text: If $Z$ is empty, then $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$ is affine and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is finite (the zero ring is a finite $k$-module), and step 3 applies. Otherwise $Z$ is nonempty and its underlying topological space has dimension at most zero by hypothesis, so by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] every local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ has Krull dimension at most zero, i.e. $\dim Z\le0$ in the sense of [def-pc-dimension]. Hence the existing algebraic zero-dimensional finiteness lemma [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite] applies to the finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ (step 1). It gives that $Z$ is affine and that $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is finite.

Applying the finite-over-a-field global-sections lemma [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] to this finite structure morphism identifies $Z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and shows that $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$.
